learning_objective: 🎯 Learn the WHO definition of health, explore the dimensions of well-being, understand balanced nutrition, and discover healthy lifestyle practices!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: According to the World Health Organization, health is 'a state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity.'
True health comprises multiple interconnected dimensions: Physical (body functioning), Mental (emotional resilience), Social (healthy relationships), and Spiritual (sense of purpose).
A balanced diet provides the correct proportions of macronutrients (carbohydrates for energy, proteins for muscle repair, fats for insulation) and micronutrients (vitamins and minerals for immunity).
Modern screen time and lack of physical activity lead to lifestyle diseases like obesity, diabetes, and hypertension. Daily exercise and proper sleep hygiene are vital countermeasures.

fun_activity.title: 🥗 The Plate Rainbow Audit
fun_activity.instructions: Look at your dinner plate tonight. How many distinct natural colors do you see? A healthy plate should have at least 3 colors (like green leafy vegetables, orange carrots/dal, and white rice/curd) to ensure balanced micronutrients!

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize the exact WHO definition of health verbatim—it is frequently asked in objective and short-answer questions.
📌 Differentiate clearly between 'Health' (overall state of being) and 'Wellness' (the active process of making choices toward a healthy life).
📌 Be ready to explain how water and roughage (dietary fiber), despite having no nutritional value, are critical for digestion.
quick_recap: ⭐ Carbohydrates and fats are energy-giving foods, while proteins are body-building foods.
⭐ Personal hygiene, clean water, and proper waste disposal prevent infectious diseases.
⭐ Mental health is just as important as physical health for overall academic and sports performance.
